mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized above its four-week mean (-16.0 vs -17.05), and one-week momentum in retail mobility tends to persist; the next four weeks should average higher than the last four.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to -17.05, the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week WORKPLACES drop greater than 5 points signals a new round of mobility restrictions; reduced commuting suppresses weekday retail-and-recreation footfall over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES t-0w -20.0 vs t-1w -13.7, a 6.3-point drop
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES drops more than 5 points week-on-week, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rebounds above -20 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 14, residents shift to local outdoor activity that spills over into nearby retail-and-recreation; this interaction lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: When PARKS > -20 and RESIDENTIAL > 14, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, persistent transit aversion (TRANSIT below -25) and workplace contraction reduce discretionary trips, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
failure_condition: In tightening-restrictions weeks with TRANSIT < -25, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is positive and rising (3.7 at t-0w), indicating essential-errand normalization; this normalization broadens into discretionary retail over four weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 1.4 to 3.7 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining positive.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week PARKS increase greater than 5 points while TRANSIT remains below -25 signals outdoor-substitution trips that increase retail-and-recreation visits over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week and TRANSIT < -25
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS t-0w -15.9 vs t-1w -23.7, a 7.8-point rise
failure_condition: When PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week and TRANSIT < -25, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than its prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: High RESIDENTIAL (>14) combined with falling WORKPLACES (below -18) locks in work-from-home routines, cutting weekday retail trips; RETAIL_REC falls over two weeks.
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL > 14 and WORKPLACES < -18, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is greater than or equal to the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening, positive GROCERY_PHARM (>3.0) combined with a PARKS rebound signals restored broad mobility; retail-and-recreation follows with a four-week rise above its last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM t-0w 3.7 above 3.0 and PARKS t-0w -15.9 above t-1w -23.7
failure_condition: In reopening weeks with GROCERY_PHARM > 3.0 and a PARKS week-on-week rise, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.
